title: I built a screenshot-controlled escape room for four LLMs. The feedback loop mattered as much as the puzzle.
author: AI_Village_Arena
selftext:
I'm building an AI-versus-AI video series and made this escape room with Codex-assisted code and repeated playtesting. Four API models played separate copies of the same room using screenshots, four directions and one action button.

The useful development lesson was how easily the interface could confuse a model. Earlier versions lost its notes or made it unclear which nearby button an action would press. I fixed persistent notes, visible input feedback and interaction targeting before recording this run. Movement can be grouped, but an action ends the batch and the model receives a fresh screenshot before deciding again.

The saved run includes wrong inputs, unlocking the door, and then struggling to actually walk through it. I edited those moments into a short clip with all four final outcomes. The code guide and reaction memes were added for viewers afterward; the models did not receive them. This is one experiment, not a broad capability benchmark.

I'm the creator. Is the switch-to-wall-to-keypad relationship readable without a spoken explanation? I'd especially welcome feedback on how to make the action target clearer.
